exhibition_placements.caption: One leg advances as the tall torso remains rigid. The missing head and arms belong to Giacometti’s conceived form; the courtyard and plinth belong to this capture of the Venice bronze.

Michael holds the sword of a defender and the scales used to weigh souls. Andrea della Robbia’s glazed relief turns a church entrance into an image of protection and judgment. This recording preserves its front; the wall-facing reverse is inaccessible.

Silvio Dolce’s plaster carries an ancient pose from a Roman marble into a twentieth-century teaching collection. Its bow is absent from the physical cast. The association with Lysippos concerns the ancient type, rather than the maker of this plaster.

The grain follows the reclining body through its rounded masses and openings. Moore’s elmwood figure makes the material’s growth visible beside the forms he carved into it. The soft texture of the recording remains distinct from the physical wood.
